green = where another square's centre can still be; GREY STIPPLE = undecided (clearance within the margin), NOT
feasible; grey DIAGONAL HATCH = pockets too narrow for any square; white = certified blocked; tags = how many
squares can reach each corner/slot, with the witnessed free meeters drawn in thin black
FEASIBLE-CENTRE REGION on a 194x194 grid of pitch 0.01998 (<= 0.02) x 36 tilts; both verdicts carry the Lipschitz margin m =
0.02956 = pitch*sqrt2/2 + (sqrt2/2)*(dtheta/2), so GREEN is a CERTIFIED inner approximation (every point of a green cell admits a
feasible tilt) and WHITE a CERTIFIED outer one (no point admits any tilt). The GREY STIPPLE between them is UNDECIDED at this
resolution -- the clearance falls within the margin, so those centres are NOT shown feasible and must not be read as free; a
stippled strip beside H is exactly the case where the all-tilt map against H's actual poses may have no feasible centre at all.
Certified-free (green) area 1.3128; a further 0.5068 is undecided. Sampled confirmation, 10^4 each at 360 tilts with an independent
SAT: green hits 0, blocked hits 0.
WITNESSED FREE MEETERS: 0 drawn (thin black outlines beside the lane tag, with how far each reaches into the cell). These are
SAMPLED poses from A157's screen of A141's UNDECIDED slot cells (a free pose, and a disjoint PAIR where the sample found one) and
A141's T5 two-crowd witness on the k0 corners. A tag's lane line prints BOTH bounds: `ub` is the certified upper bound, `lb` the
number of free meeters the sample actually found, `M` the conditioned meeters (`?` = not certified exactly). A hairline grazer -- a
witnessed square reaching a few thousandths into the cell -- refutes a reading that the corner is unreachable, and is invisible
unless it is drawn.
DISK BOUND (the shortcut): a unit square contains the disk of radius 1/2 about its centre, so the 5 remaining centres carry
disjoint half-unit disks inside the container, all with centres in green+undecided. That region dilated by 1/2 and clipped to the
container has area 8.2532, so at most 10 more unit squares fit — the budget is 5, so this alone does not kill the node.

PANEL G is the GEOMETRY of the hypothesis: the container, the hypothesis squares with their certified cores, and the shaded set of centres where one further unit square can still be placed at SOME tilt. Nothing in panel G comes from an LP; it is what the case hypothesis alone
forces. This is the panel to read for a shortcut.

PANEL S is the LP RELAXATION's dual support: a fractional measure, one placement per column, shaded by dual weight. Its squares OVERLAP each other and sometimes the hypothesis — that is the relaxation's slack, not a packing, and a column drawn red is one the geometry of panel G
already forbids.

PANEL N is a REAL PACKING: the nearest configuration of eleven pairwise interior-disjoint unit squares to this node's support, minimised over its own side s*. If s* > s0 the configuration does not fit in the certified container; the square names are the labels used everywhere
else.

CONVENTIONS — BODIES are filled; CERTIFIED CORES are filled purple (K'(B), A132) or outlined (a pin's exact core, A135); SCHEMATIC regions (centre boxes, the pin-clipped box, lane cells, guard lines) are THIN DASHED and are never square bodies. One style per object: the stock

and exact AXIS cores are captioned, not drawn. In panel G a centre is GREEN = certified free, GREY STIPPLE = undecided (clearance within the margin, NOT feasible), WHITE = certified blocked; the grey DIAGONAL HATCH is a separate object, a pocket too narrow for any square. Thin
black outlines beside a lane tag are WITNESSED free meeters (sampled poses), with how far each reaches into the cell.
